You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The test `['org.apache.commons.lang.WordUtilsTest.testAbbreviate()']` failed.
The test looks like:

```java
366 :     public void testAbbreviate() {
367 :         // check null and empty are returned respectively
370 : 
371 :         // test upper limit
377 : 
378 :         // test upper limit + append string
384 : 
385 :         // test lower value
390 :         assertEquals("0123456789", WordUtils.abbreviate("0123456789", 15, 20, null));
401 :     }
```

Current bug report: {'summary': 'WordUtils.abbreviate bug when lower is greater than str.length', 'description': 'In WordUtils.abbreviate, upper is adjusted to the length of the string, then to lower.  \nBut lower is never adjusted to the length of the string, so if lower is greater than str.lengt(), upper will be too...  \nThen, str.substring(0, upper) throw a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException\nThe fix is to adjust lower to the length of the string\n'}

Recent bug reports (SBERT retrieval results with similarity): [{'similarity': 0.36, 'summary': 'Cut out middle part of a String', 'description': 'It would be handy to have a String method that cuts out the middle part of a String such that as much as possible is kept from the start and end of the String, but the middle part is replaced by an ellipsis "..."\nBeOS had a function like this, but it\'s poorly documented, missing examples:  \n<http://www.beunited.org/bebook/The%20Support%20Kit/String.html#Truncate(>)\ne.g. :  \nA very long text with u'}, {'similarity': 0.31, 'summary': "EqualsBuilder don't compare BigDecimals correctly", 'description': 'When comparing a BigDecimal, the comparing is made using equals, not compareTo, which is more appropriate in the case of BigDecimal.'}, {'similarity': 0.46, 'summary': 'StringUtils.length(String) returns null-safe length', 'description': 'Create a new method: Null-safe StringUtils.length(String). Patch attached for the record. Will commit soon unless someone thinks this is a bad idea.'}]

The `WordUtils.abbreviate` method from the Apache Commons Lang library takes a string `str`, lower and upper bounds `lower` and `upper`, and a string to append at the end. It adjusts the upper and lower bounds based on the length of the input string `str` and then abbreviates the string accordingly.

The issue reported states that when the lower bound is greater than the length of the input string `str`, the upper bound is also set to this value, leading to an index out of bounds exception when trying to abbreviate the string.

By looking at the method implementation, we can see that the upper bound is correctly adjusted if it is greater than the length of the string. However, the lower bound is not adjusted in a similar way.

To diagnose the bug step by step:
1. The method first performs initial parameter checks and adjusts the upper bound if needed.
2. It then checks if the upper bound is less than the lower bound and raises it to be equal to the lower bound.
3. The method then attempts to find the index of a space starting from the lower bound.
4. If no space is found or the space index is beyond the upper bound, it abbreviates the string by taking a substring from 0 to the upper bound.
5. If a space is found within the bounds, it abbreviates the string up to the space index.
6. Finally, it appends the `appendToEnd` string if required and returns the resulting abbreviation.

The bug occurs because the lower bound `lower` is not adjusted when it is greater than the length of the input string `str`, leading to an incorrect calculation of the substring index and causing a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

To fix the bug, the lower bound `lower` should also be adjusted to be equal to the length of the input string `str` if it is greater than the length.

Now, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed based on this diagnosis.
org.apache.commons.lang.WordUtils.abbreviate(java.lang.String,int,int,java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
